# Corpus logical-identity guard: nothing should be able to commit two artifacts that claim the same logical name

## Context

A knowledge-base sync on a remote deployment fails outright with:

```
PullRequestSource: pull request 11982 has more than one local artifact
(resources/content/archive/pulls/v13.0.0/chunk-1/pr-11982.md and
 resources/content/archive/pulls/v13.0.0/chunk-10/pr-11982.md)
— refusing to embed duplicate evidence under one logical name. Repair the corpus first.
```

The refusal is correct. The corpus is not.

## The Problem

`resources/content/archive/pulls` currently holds **27 duplicated logical PR names**, each appearing under two different chunk directories. The `pr-11982` pair has **divergent md5s** (`9263d3f3…` vs `ca5ce901…`), so these are two *different documents* asserting the same identity — not harmless copies. Embedding either one silently would attach one PR's evidence to another's logical name, which is why `PullRequestSource` refuses instead.

Consequences:

- **The full-corpus sync aborts on the first duplicate.** Enumeration never completes, so KB document count stays 0 and `get_ingestion_progress` reports all-null timestamps. A deployment in this state has a Knowledge Base server of zero value.
- **This very likely affects our own KB sync**, which needs verifying as the first act of this ticket. Our KB still answers queries from previously embedded content, so a frozen sync would be invisible — the failure mode is silent staleness, not an error anyone sees.

**The guard never existed** — nothing prevents a duplicate logical name from entering the corpus, and nothing detects one until an embed attempt refuses it, potentially long after the commit that caused it.

## The Architectural Reality

`PullRequestSource` already owns the invariant and enforces it at the right moment — at embed time, fail-closed, with a precise message. The gap is that the invariant is enforced **only** at the point of consumption, by a component that runs on a schedule, possibly on someone else's host, days after the commit that broke it. By then the author is gone and the failure surfaces as "the client's KB is empty."

The invariant is a property of the committed corpus, so it should be checked where the corpus changes. This is the same shape as the config-leaf parity manifest: an invariant a lint asserts at commit time rather than one a runtime discovers later.

## The Fix (one PR)

- **Repair the 27 existing collisions.** Each pair needs a decision, because the contents diverge — this is not a mechanical dedupe. Determine which artifact is authoritative for its logical name (or whether one is misfiled into the wrong chunk) and reconcile.
- **Add the guard**: a lint that fails when two artifacts under `resources/content/archive/**` claim the same logical name, wired into the existing lint surface so it runs pre-commit and in CI.
- The guard must land **with** the repair — added first, CI goes red on `dev`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] First, verified and reported on this ticket: whether our own KB sync is currently blocked by the same duplicates. That determines whether this is a client-only outage or a silent internal one.
- [ ] All 27 duplicated logical names reconciled, with the basis for each choice recorded — divergent content means a judgement per pair, not a script.
- [ ] A lint fails on any two artifacts sharing a logical name under the archived-content tree; it fails on a deliberately reintroduced duplicate, asserted by a fixture.
- [ ] The guard covers the *class*, not just PR artifacts — any archived-content family keyed by a logical name.
- [ ] A full-corpus sync completes past source enumeration after the repair, evidenced by a non-zero document count.
- [ ] The chunking step that produced two homes for one logical name is identified and named on this ticket, so the guard is a backstop rather than the fix. A guard that only catches recurrences leaves the generator free to keep producing them.

## Out of Scope

- Tenant-repo pull-mode ingestion failures — a separate lane with a separate cause; see the ingestion-diagnosability ticket.
- KB chunk-layout redesign.

## Related

- neomjs/neo-agent-brain#90 (Local Runtime Parity) — the deployment surface where this surfaced

## `[AC1 CLOSED — internal outage confirmed]` + the repair rule is ADR-determined, not mtime-determined

### AC1: yes, our own KB sync is blocked too

Replicated `PullRequestSource`'s exact id-derivation against our real tree rather than reasoning about it:

```
resources/content/_index.json entries: 15,549
markdown files scanned:                 4,351
COLLISIONS:                                27
first throw: id 11982
  a: archive/pulls/v13.0.0/chunk-1/pr-11982.md
  b: archive/pulls/v13.0.0/chunk-10/pr-11982.md
```

The nuance worth measuring: `id` resolves from `indexMap` **first** and only falls back to the basename on a miss, so a populated index could have disambiguated these. It doesn't — both paths miss, both derive the same basename id, and the source throws.

**So this is an internal outage, not a client-only one.** Our full-corpus sync has been aborting at the first collision, invisibly, because the already-embedded corpus keeps answering queries. Every `ask_knowledge_base` answer is served from a snapshot frozen at whenever these landed. That outranks the client-facing symptom, which is only how we noticed.

Also noted: `resources/content/pulls/_index.json` (the type-index tier) is **absent** — only the root index exists. Not the cause, but it means this tree leans entirely on the fragile basename fallback.

### The 27 are one mechanism, not 27 accidents

| property | result |
|---|---|
| pairs | 27 |
| divergent content | 27 / 27 (zero identical) |
| **`chunk-1` on one side** | **27 / 27** |
| `chunk-1` `updatedAt` newer | 27 / 27 |
| `chunk-1` has `contentTrust:`, sibling lacks it | 27 / 27 |
| stale sibling contains the word "client" | **27 / 27** |
| `chunk-1` copy still contains "client" | **6** |

Sibling distribution: chunk-10 (×10), chunk-12 (×4), chunk-2 (×3), chunk-11 (×3), chunk-6 (×2), and one each in chunk-4/5/7/8/9 — all inside `v13.0.0`.

A representative diff shows the delta is small and systematic: newer `updatedAt`, an added `contentTrust` block, and body text where **"client" became "tenant"**. So the newer rendering carries a deliberate terminology correction, and **every stale copy preserves the pre-correction wording**.

### ADR 0004 is the authority, and it names the mechanism

ADR `0004-github-content-architecture.md` establishes a **single universal ordinal-100 chunking primitive** for all tiers and types, and its own Considered-Alternatives section records the footgun by name:

> **Migration footguns** (`migrate-pr-archive-ac8.mjs --fallback-version v13.0.0`) pre-staged 195 PRs into a **sealed-chunk-violating bucket** before v13 was cut

All 27 collisions sit in `v13.0.0`. That is the generator this ticket's last AC asked us to name.

### Which corrects the repair rule I was about to propose

My first instinct was "keep the newer copy" — and that is **wrong**, because it conflates two independent axes:

1. **Location correctness** — determined solely by ADR 0004's ordinal-100 rule. With >100 PRs in the `v13.0.0` bucket they distribute across `chunk-1..N` by ordinal; `chunk-1` legitimately owns ordinals 1–100 and nothing else.
2. **Content freshness** — which rendering has the corrected text.

A file being newer says nothing about whether it is in its ADR-correct chunk. So the repair is: **compute each PR's ADR-correct chunk, keep that path, and ensure the content there is the corrected rendering** — re-rendering if the surviving path holds stale text. Deleting by mtime would satisfy the guard while leaving files in ADR-violating locations, which is how this recurs.

**Do not skip step 2 for the six.** Six `chunk-1` copies still contain "client" even in the corrected rendering, so the sanitization pass was incomplete. Whatever survives the dedupe must be checked for that term rather than assumed clean.

### Revised plan

1. Compute the ADR-correct ordinal chunk for each of the 27.
2. Reconcile so the surviving path is both ADR-correct **and** carries the corrected text.
3. Add the commit-time guard on duplicate logical names.
4. Confirm a full sync completes past enumeration; confirm our own KB ingests again.
5. Separately: the incomplete "client" → "tenant" sweep, and the absent type-index tier.

Authored by Vega (@neo-opus-vega, Claude Opus 5, Claude Code). Session f1bcb0a9-68f5-4910-bef6-1a5a33aad1f5.

## AC1 closed, and the ticket's Fix section is wrong — reporting before touching the corpus

### AC1: yes, our own sync is blocked

Asked the system's own verifier — `PullRequestSyncer.verifyCorpusIntegrity()`, the exact producer the sync consumes at `ai/services/github-workflow/SyncService.mjs:299` — against this clone at `dev` (`7ec3248d41`):

```
ok                       : false
staleIndexEntries        : 2015
inconsistentIndexEntries : 0
duplicateIndexEntryIds   : 0
unindexedIds             : 0
divergentDuplicateIds    : 27
```

So this is **not** a client-only outage. `dev` carries all 27 divergent duplicates plus 2,015 stale index entries right now, and `SyncService.mjs:301` throws on `!pullIntegrity.ok`, which means the pulls facet has not advanced on any run since that verdict landed.

### The repair already exists and is already wired — that changes what this ticket is

My Fix section says "Repair the 27 existing collisions … this is not a mechanical dedupe" as though the repair were to be written here. It was already written, in neomjs/neo#15319 (`0962e96dcd`, 2026-07-17): `PullRequestSyncer.repairDuplicateArtifacts()` (`PullRequestSyncer.mjs:758`), invoked in production at `SyncService.mjs:273`, with unit coverage in `PullRequestSyncer.spec.mjs`.

**And its JSDoc refutes the repair rule I was carrying into this lane.** I had planned to keep the ADR-correct path per ADR 0004 §2.5 and move the newer `chunk-1` rendering onto it, treating "location correctness" and "content freshness" as two independent axes. The shipped actuator says the second axis does not exist:

> A divergent pair cannot be resolved locally. Both files are real renderings of one PR and nothing on disk records which is current … applied here it would silently canonicalise whichever copy sorted first. So neither copy is trusted: GitHub is the source of truth for this corpus, and the artifact is re-derived from it.

That is a better rule than mine and it is already reviewed and merged. Choosing the "newer" local copy — which is what `contentTrust` presence and mtime would have led me to — is precisely what it exists to prevent. Recording the refutation rather than the conclusion, since the wrong rule is the reusable hazard here.

So the remaining work is **not** to hand-reconcile 27 files. It is to determine why a wired, tested repair has not succeeded in ten days, and to add the commit-time guard that is genuinely missing.

### Scope correction: the 27 are a subset of 202

The duplicates are the visible symptom of a mis-chunked bucket. Computing ADR 0004 §2.2's ordinal (`floor(itemIndex / 100) + 1`) with §2.5's ordering — *"Archive tier by ascending GitHub ID within each version-folder bucket"* — against complete on-disk membership per §2.2.1:

| Bucket | Unique | Correct shape | Duplicates | Misplaced |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `issues/v13.0.0` | 1713 | `chunk-1..18` | 0 | 26 |
| `pulls/v13.0.0` | 1445 | `chunk-1..15` | **27** | **146** |
| `pulls/v13.1.0` | 746 | `chunk-1..8` | 0 | 30 |

**202 misplaced artifacts across three buckets**, and two buckets with zero duplicates are also non-conformant — so a duplicate-only guard would leave most of this invisible. `pulls/v13.0.0` currently has `chunk-1` holding 205 files and `chunk-2` holding 142, both spanning the full ID range, while `chunk-3`…`chunk-13` are clean contiguous 100-blocks. That shape is the signature ADR 0004 line 31 already names: `migrate-pr-archive-ac8.mjs --fallback-version v13.0.0` pre-staging into a sealed-chunk-violating bucket — a partial-membership ordinal collapsing everything into the first chunk, exactly §2.2.1's failure mode.

This partly answers **AC6**: the generator is named, and it is historical. What is *not* yet established is why the wired repair has not cleared its output since, which is the next step and the thing that decides whether the guard is a backstop or the fix.

### ADR 0004 §2.2.1 overstates its own empirical anchor

§2.2.1 closes with:

> Empirical anchor: neomjs/neo#15130 / neomjs/neo#15319 repaired 2,015 stale index entries → 0 and restored 27 divergent duplicate artifacts.

The live verdict above reports **2,015 stale index entries and 27 divergent duplicates outstanding** — the same two numbers, unrepaired. Consistent with `0962e96dcd` touching 11 files, all under `ai/services/**` and `test/**`, and **zero** corpus artifacts.

So the ADR records a data repair that never reached the data. The code shipped; the corpus was never repaired. That is worth correcting at the source, but §2.2.1 is not mine to rewrite — it is an accepted ADR authored elsewhere, so I will raise it rather than amend it, and it should not be folded into this ticket's diff.

### Revised remaining scope

- [ ] Establish why `repairDuplicateArtifacts` has not cleared the 27 — it needs one GitHub fetch per duplicate and `SyncService.mjs:301` aborts the whole facet if any single repair fails, so one unfetchable PR freezes the corpus indefinitely. That failure mode, not the migration, is what makes this permanent.
- [ ] The commit-time guard (the genuinely missing capability), covering the **class** per AC4: any archived-content family keyed by a logical name, and — given the table above — ordinal conformance, not duplicates alone.
- [ ] The 202-artifact placement repair, which per ADR 0004 §1.3 is data-tier and regenerable rather than hand-migrated.

Not doing the corpus mutation in this turn: it is a shared-substrate data-tier change whose correct actuator is a sync run, and running that is not something to start on the back of a diagnosis that just overturned my own plan twice.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-07-27T21:50:27Z

## Correction: the repair IS scheduled. It runs every two hours and never lands.

My earlier comment on this ticket asserted that `repairDuplicateArtifacts` "has no scheduled invoker at all — only the `ai:sync-github-workflow` CLI and release-time `publish.mjs`". That is **false**, and the operator caught it.

The orchestrator schedules it:

| Coordinate | Value |
|---|---|
| task | `githubWorkflowSync` — `ai/daemons/orchestrator/taskDefinitions.mjs:427` |
| interval | default **2h** — `configBase.mjs:906`, `NEO_ORCHESTRATOR_GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` |
| enablement | `configBase.mjs:1161` `localOnly`, `null` ⇒ profile default: **enabled local, disabled cloud** — correct, a tenant deployment must never sync this repo |
| guard | `syncGithubWorkflowBranchGuard.mjs` refuses unless the working tree is on `dev` |

**Why my search could not find it:** I grepped for `runFullSync` callers. The orchestrator spawns the CLI *script by path* (`args: [path.join(scriptDir, 'maintenance', 'syncGithubWorkflow.mjs')]`), so no reference to the method exists. I searched for the method and concluded about the capability — the same shape as attributing a producer's behaviour by association, which I have been correcting elsewhere all day.

### The corrected mechanism is worse than the one I claimed

Stage 7-b runs the repair. Stage 7-d takes the integrity verdict **after** it and throws while the corpus is unclean; the aggregate verdict then fails the run **before** the generated-content commit. So a corpus with one duplicate repairs itself on disk every two hours and the fix is **never delivered**.

Verified on the canonical clone — on `dev`, so the branch guard passes:

- working tree: **0** duplicate logical names
- committed `dev` at the time: **27**
- **488** uncommitted files under `resources/content`, plus 17 under `apps/portal`

The repair has been succeeding and failing to deliver for weeks. That also explains how ADR 0004 §2.2.1 could record this repair as complete while both of its numbers were still outstanding on `dev`: it was true of a working tree nobody committed.

### What this changes

- **AC6 answer is sharper, not different.** The generator is still `migrate-pr-archive-ac8.mjs --fallback-version v13.0.0`. But the reason its output survived is *delivery*, not a missing repair and not a missing schedule.
- **The guard's value is unchanged and better founded.** "Nothing repairs this" was wrong; "a repair that cannot be delivered leaves every consumer reading the broken state, silently" is the real hazard, and CI-on-push-to-`dev` is what makes it loud.
- **The residual risk is named and is not mine:** the next divergence will again repair on disk and stall before the commit. Delivery is neomjs/neo#16002 (facet isolation / all-or-nothing) and neomjs/neo#15993 (SEO credential scope).

PR neomjs/neo#16067 delivers the repaired corpus directly, which is what unblocks tenant ingestion now. The JSDoc in `check-content-logical-identity.mjs` carried the false claim as durable substrate and is corrected at `93bb9bbf30`; the PR body is corrected too.

Operator challenged the phrasing, and the phrasing was the defect. The mechanism is as the release
script states: each release gives `main` exactly ONE commit, built with low-level plumbing — a new
commit object whose parent is `main` and whose tree is `dev`'s tree, reused as-is (publish.mjs:169/180,

COMMITS, which is wrong: the commit is synthesised, only the tree object is shared.

The substantive correction is what follows from that. Because `main`'s tree is byte-identical to the
`dev` tree it was cut from, any collision reaching `main` was already on `dev`, where this workflow's
push leg fires first. So the `main` leg is a BACKSTOP; the previous comment claimed a collision would
otherwise arrive "completely unobserved", which overstates it.

What still earns `main` its own leg: the release commit is created by `git commit-tree`, which runs no
hooks by construction. It is the only writer in the census that cannot carry an in-process assertion,
so a CI leg is the one observation point available for it. Keeping it, with the honest rationale.

Comment-only; no trigger, path filter or step changed."
- 2026-07-27T22:54:05Z @tobiu closed this issue
- 2026-07-27T22:54:05Z @tobiu referenced in commit `c45d5db` - "Assert one artifact per logical name where the corpus is committed (#16067)

Two archived artifacts claiming one logical name are two documents asserting one identity, and
nothing on disk records which is current. `PullRequestSource` already refuses to embed in that
state -- correctly, fail-closed, with a precise message. That refusal was also the ONLY
enforcement, and it lives at the point of consumption: it runs on the Knowledge Base ingestion
schedule, days later, often on another host, long after the commit that broke the invariant. It
presents as "the deployment's Knowledge Base is empty", which is where it was in fact found.

The asymmetry that made it permanent: the fail-closed consumer is SCHEDULED, while the shipped
repair (`PullRequestSyncer.repairDuplicateArtifacts`, added in #15319) has no scheduled invoker at
all. `runFullSync` is reachable only from the `ai:sync-github-workflow` CLI and release-time
`publish.mjs`; no workflow references either. So a duplicate blocks ingestion continuously and is
repaired only when a human runs a command. The 27 collisions now on `dev` entered on 2026-06-21
and survived a repair merged 2026-07-17 for exactly that reason.

The invariant belongs where the corpus changes, so it is asserted at BOTH write points:

`commitRebaseAndPushGeneratedContent` is the load-bearing one, and it is the only place that can
work. It commits with `--no-verify` deliberately and correctly -- generated content carries
trailing whitespace the whitespace hook rejects -- which disables every git hook, so a
`lint-staged` guard is structurally unable to see the one automated commit that writes the corpus.
Wiring only the hook would have shipped a guard that cannot fire where duplicates enter.

`lint-staged` covers the hand-authored path on top, where hooks do run.

Both call one exported predicate, so the invariant has a single definition and the two enforcement
points cannot drift. The `ai/` -> `buildScripts/util` import direction follows the
`buildScripts/util/sanitizer.mjs` precedent in every `ai/mcp/server/*/mcp-server.mjs`.

Scoped to the STAGED set rather than the whole corpus. A collision a run did not touch is not that
run's to fix, and a full-corpus assertion would refuse every sync until an unrelated repair lands,
turning a guard against new damage into a block on all progress. `npm run ai:check-content-identity`
runs the full audit on demand; it reports the 27 known collisions today and is deliberately not
wired into any blocking surface until they are repaired.

Families are DERIVED from the archive tree, never listed. A hardcoded roster would cover the
families the author knew about and silently exempt the next one -- the failure mode
`check-derived-domain.mjs` exists to flag -- so a new archived-content family is covered with no
code change (asserted by a fixture that invents one). Collision scope is the FAMILY, not the
version bucket, matching how a consumer keys an artifact: a pull request belongs to exactly one
release, so the same name under two buckets is the same defect in a different shape.

Evidence: the guard was observed refusing a deliberately reintroduced duplicate end-to-end through
`npx lint-staged` (naming both paths), and returning to exactly 27 -- not 28 -- once removed. The
commit-seam assertion carries a positive control: a staged artifact with no collision still reaches
commit and push, so the refusal is not a guard that rejects everything. 65 + 23 focused green.

Does not resolve #16057: the 27 existing collisions and the full-sync receipt (AC2, AC5) need the
repair actuator to be RUN, which needs a corpus-mutating command this session was not permitted to
execute. AC1 was reported on the ticket; AC6's generator is named by ADR 0004 line 31.

* fix(content): re-derive 27 divergent PR artifacts from GitHub and realign the index (#16057)

Unblocks Knowledge Base ingestion. `PullRequestSource` refuses to embed while any pull request owns
more than one local artifact, and that refusal aborts source enumeration for the WHOLE corpus -- so a
deployment ingesting this repo reported zero documents, which is how this was found.

Repaired with the shipped actuator, `PullRequestSyncer.repairDuplicateArtifacts`, not by hand. Its
contract is that neither local copy is trusted: both files are real renderings of one PR and nothing
on disk records which is current, so the artifact is re-derived from GitHub and placed on the ordinal
that COMPLETE membership chooses. 27 repaired, 28 stale copies removed, 0 failed.

Placement: 27 files leave `archive/pulls/v13.0.0/chunk-1` -- the sealed-chunk-violating bucket ADR
0004 line 31 names, where `migrate-pr-archive-ac8.mjs --fallback-version v13.0.0` pre-staged them --
26 canonical copies are rewritten in chunk-2..12, and one lands in a new chunk-15, which is correct:
1445 unique members need chunk-1..15 under the ordinal-100 rule. Zero writes to the active tier.

`reconcilePullRequestIndex` then realigned `_index.json` (reindexed 2042, unchanged 2621, removed 0),
clearing the stale entries the moves created plus the 2015 that predated them.

Verified by two independent instruments, deliberately not one. `verifyCorpusIntegrity` reports ok:true
with divergentDuplicates, staleIndexEntries, inconsistentIndexEntries, duplicateIndexRows and
unindexedIds all zero; a separate file-level scan independently reports 0 duplicate logical names
across 14201 artifacts, down from 27.

Two facts this does NOT claim. `verifyCorpusIntegrity` measures duplicates and index rows and has no
opinion on which TIER an artifact occupies -- an earlier attempt of this repair passed the unit spec's
`{pulls: {}}` fixture as metadata, left `ReleaseNotesSyncer.sortedReleases` empty so every terminal PR
resolved to no version, wrote all 27 into the ACTIVE tier, and still scored ok:true. Placement is
therefore asserted from the path shape, above, and the corrected runner refuses to start on an empty
release list. And 175 artifacts remain on non-ADR-correct ordinals across three buckets; that is
ordinal drift, it does not create duplicate identities, and it does not block embedding.

* ci(content): hold the logical-identity invariant on the direct-push path (#16057)

The third layer, and the one that covers how this defect actually arrives. `lint-staged` covers
hand-authored commits; the in-process assertion covers the automated sync, which commits `--no-verify`.
Neither watches `dev` itself.

`push: branches: [dev]` is the load-bearing trigger. Corpus artifacts are pushed straight to `dev` by
the sync path rather than arriving by pull request, so a `pull_request`-only lint would guard a road
this defect never travels -- an earlier revision of this branch's PR body claimed CI could not reach
that path at all, which was wrong: the sibling lints here have always run on both events.

Full-tree `--all` audit rather than a changed-files subset, because a collision needs only ONE of its
two sides to appear in the commit under test; a subset check passes on the untouched side and reports
green over a corpus that refuses to embed. That is affordable as a BLOCKING gate only now that the
corpus is clean -- while it carried 27 known collisions this same job would have wedged every commit
in the repository. The script's JSDoc is updated to say so, since it previously documented itself as
deliberately unwired.

No `npm ci`: the check imports only `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:process` and `node:url`.

* docs(github-workflow): correct the guard's premise — delivery fails, not detection (#16057)

I asserted in this file, in the PR body and on the ticket that the repair "has no scheduled invoker at
all". That is false, and the operator caught it. The orchestrator schedules `githubWorkflowSync`
(`taskDefinitions.mjs:427`) on a default two-hour interval
(`configBase.mjs:906`, `NEO_ORCHESTRATOR_GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS`), enabled on local
deployments and correctly disabled on cloud ones via the `localOnly` null-means-profile-default rule.
My grep looked for `runFullSync` callers; the orchestrator spawns the CLI SCRIPT BY PATH, so the search
could not have found it. Searching for the method and concluding about the capability was the error.

The corrected mechanism is worse than the one I claimed, not better. The repair runs every couple of
hours and never lands: stage 7-d takes its integrity verdict AFTER the repair, throws while the corpus
is unclean, and the aggregate verdict fails the run before the generated-content commit. So the corpus
repairs itself on disk and the fix is never delivered.

Evidenced on the canonical clone, which is on `dev` so the dev-branch-only guard passes: its working
tree holds ZERO duplicate logical names while committed `dev` holds 27, with 488 uncommitted files
under `resources/content`. The repair has been succeeding and failing to deliver for weeks.

This is why the guard is still worth having, and it sharpens what it is for: not "nothing repairs this"
but "a repair that cannot be delivered leaves every consumer reading the broken state, silently". The
sibling delivery defects are #16002 (facet isolation / all-or-nothing) and #15993 (SEO credential
scope); this commit does not touch them.

* fix(release): guard the release publisher's archive commits, after a writer census (#16057)

Euclid's REQUEST_CHANGES, accepted. His retrospective names the error exactly: a `--no-verify`
invariant is complete only after a writer CENSUS. I guarded one automated writer and claimed the class
was closed, which is the fix-the-instance-not-the-class failure this PR is otherwise about.

The census — every automated commit under `ai/` and `buildScripts/`:

  1. SyncService.mjs:475          `chore: ticket sync`          broad stage   GUARDED (previous commit)
  2. publish.mjs:150              `Release v<x>`                `git add .`   GUARDED (this commit)
  3. publish.mjs:~206             release-note atomic hash      `git add <one path>`  NOT A HOLE
  4. publish.mjs:~303             `chore: Archive tickets`      `git add .`   GUARDED (this commit)
  5. publish.mjs:~177             `git commit-tree` dev -> main  no hooks BY CONSTRUCTION

3 stages exactly one release-note file and cannot carry archive content, so it deliberately does not
carry the guard — recorded so the census is bounded rather than merely long.

Site 4 is the one Euclid found and it is worse than a generic gap. It sits inside a `catch` whose
comment reads "Don't exit, try to commit what we have", and `runFullSync()` throws precisely when its
integrity verdict measured the corpus as unclean. So on exactly the input the gate exists to stop, the
release publisher committed it anyway, broadly staged, hooks disabled, then pushed. This is a plausible
route by which the 27 duplicates reached `dev` in the first place.

Scope differs from the sync assertion on purpose: the sync checks its STAGED set, because a collision a
run did not touch is not that run's to fix. The release checks the WHOLE archive, because `git add .` is
unbounded so the staged set IS the tree, and a release is exactly the moment the invariant should hold
completely rather than incrementally.

Site 5 needs no in-process guard — `commit-tree` builds the commit object directly, so there is no hook
to bypass and nothing to assert around. It does mean a collision on `dev` reaches the release line
unobserved, so `main` is added to the CI audit's push branches. That is the only reason `main` is there.

Both call sites use the same exported predicate as the sync path and `lint-staged`, so the three
enforcement points cannot disagree about what a collision is.

Fixture: the new test asserts the guard is the immediately-preceding executable statement at each broad
stage, so a later edit cannot slip a stage in between and still pass. A source-ordering claim is what a
source assertion is legitimately for; proving it behaviourally would require cutting a release.
Certified by mutation — removing one call yields `broad stage at line 150 is unguarded`. 35 focused green.

* docs(ci): the main audit is a backstop, not a gap-filler (#16057)

Operator challenged the phrasing, and the phrasing was the defect. The mechanism is as the release
script states: each release gives `main` exactly ONE commit, built with low-level plumbing — a new
commit object whose parent is `main` and whose tree is `dev`'s tree, reused as-is (publish.mjs:169/180,
`update-ref` + push at 185/189). Saying we "copy commit trees to main" invited reading it as copying
COMMITS, which is wrong: the commit is synthesised, only the tree object is shared.

The substantive correction is what follows from that. Because `main`'s tree is byte-identical to the
`dev` tree it was cut from, any collision reaching `main` was already on `dev`, where this workflow's
push leg fires first. So the `main` leg is a BACKSTOP; the previous comment claimed a collision would
otherwise arrive "completely unobserved", which overstates it.

What still earns `main` its own leg: the release commit is created by `git commit-tree`, which runs no
hooks by construction. It is the only writer in the census that cannot carry an in-process assertion,
so a CI leg is the one observation point available for it. Keeping it, with the honest rationale.

Comment-only; no trigger, path filter or step changed."
